# falcon-v1.140.0 — "Hold"

The hold release. A position hold that stays bounded for an hour on **both** execution paths, judged horizontally rather than on altitude alone; the cascade transport seam published; and the root cause of the attitude ring found where no proof was looking.

## What this tag actually verifies

Nine artifacts reach `verified` at `falcon-v1.140.0`, and they are the only claims this tag carries as verified:

| requirement | what it asserts |
|---|---|
| `SWREQ-FALCON-HOLD-P01` | a stationary position hold stays bounded for 60 s on the reference gz plant |
| `SWREQ-FALCON-ENDURANCE-P01` | a position hold stays bounded for **hours**, on both the native and wasm paths |
| `SWREQ-FALCON-BATTERY-P03` | a pack that stops *reporting* in flight raises the failsafe — but only if it ever reported one |
| `SWREQ-RELAY-MIXPROOF-P01` | the MIX-P06 priority-mix bound proof holds compositionally and can fail |
| `FLEET-P01` (via `FV-RELAY-FLEET-002`) | fleet starvation is measured from jobs, and hosted contention is not reported as a dead fleet |

**Everything else below ships as code on main and is not verified by this release.** Where that matters, it is said inline.

## What this release is actually about

**The hold holds, and it is measured on the axis that matters.** The nightly endurance soak previously ran only the native path and barred only altitude — so a run that held height while drifting away passed. Clause 3 of `ENDURANCE-P01` names two axes. The soak now runs the **wasm component too** (#524), judges both paths horizontally (#525), and its floor was ratcheted from 120 s to the full 3600 s only after the hour had actually run four nights running (#523). Both paths now hold the hour. On the most recent **scheduled** run (2026-10-08, run `37764076289`, the cadence that matters rather than a dispatch), the legs report final horizontal error of **0.008–0.035 m** with peak excursion **0.016–0.071 m**, against bars of **1.0 m** and **2.0 m** — roughly thirty times the margin the bars demand. Provenance, since a cited figure should name its commit: that run executed on `8bec5fc`, and `cdf3b74` (#539) has since touched `soak.yml` — but #539 changed only the cross-job **notice** wording, no bar or threshold, so the figures measure the same bars this tag ships.

**A real filter-rate defect fixed — but not the ring.** The filters were designed for 1 kHz and stepped at 250 Hz (#488), a resampling error rather than a tuning problem. **The attitude ring itself is still open.** #270 and #398 are both open, and `SWREQ-FALCON-RATE-P05` / `FV-FALCON-RATE-002` are `implemented` and scoped **v1.142** — their fix is not on main, which is why #495 retracted an earlier "fixed" claim and #529/#538 demoted and re-scoped them. Treat the ring as an open investigation whose primary cause is understood (ESO windup under mixer saturation, measured in `bench-evidence/gz-sim/`) but whose fix has not landed.

Separately, v1.140's stale-aiding fallback was actively harmful and was **removed**: a multirotor accelerometer reads specific force along the thrust axis, so it is **never** a tilt reference in flight (#487, #483).

**The cascade transport seam ships as code — and is NOT verified by this release.** `TRANSPORT-P01` lands the framing, handshake and tick contract (#504), the cascade returns state through an observer export with a seqlock (#493), and the reference host speaks the published binding with the legacy 16/54-byte frames retired (#530). ⚠️ **For jess in particular, who specified this seam:** `SWREQ-FALCON-TRANSPORT-P01` and `FV-FALCON-TRANSPORT-001/002/003` are all `implemented`, scoped **falcon-v1.141.0**. The code is in this tag and can be built against; the seam's verification is not. Do not read this release as delivering a verified transport contract.

**The supervisor can say why** — it reports the *reason* it failsafed, not only what it did (#515). Also code-only: `SWREQ-FALCON-SUPERVISOR-P01` is `proposed` at v1.141 and blocked on jess#167, the seam reshape, so this capability is shipped but unverified.

## Verification integrity — the unglamorous half

Four gates were checking less than they appeared to, and all four are fixed in this release:

- The **Verus gate was path-filtered on Lean paths**, so it never ran on the PRs that changed Verus code (#531, issue #418). It now also **asserts it verified something**, with a floor so the assertion can fail: **281 functions, 0 errors, across 19 targets** on this release's commit, read from run `37881361372` (the figure was 270 when the assertion landed in #533). That refuted #405 outright.
- The **required verification gate had no main backstop**: nothing ever re-ran it on the merge result, so a scope filter could exclude what a PR changed and nobody would know (#535, issue #410). The backstop is **observed working, not merely configured** — its first `schedule`-event run (2026-10-09 07:58Z, run `37902164712`) swept **207 artifacts** on main and passed. That distinction matters here: a cron in a file is not evidence, and this repo's scheduled workflows are throttled by Actions well past their stated cadence.
- **`bazel.yml` enumerated its targets** instead of querying them, which is #407's cause rather than its symptom (#540).
- **`soak.yml` had been rejected by Actions since 08:56** and nothing would have told us (#507); a companion check now measures whether the nightly soak *ran*, and its very first run falsified the claim that it had (#522).

Plus: red checks are now classified **REAL / LOST / DERIVED / SUPERSEDED** instead of being read at face value (#517), a green-but-stuck PR no longer needs a human to notice it (`CIFLOW-P01`, #511), and the branch keeper no longer authors PR heads — which had silently gated every PR's CI behind manual approval (#512).

**`FLEET-002`** closes the round: the fleet monitor's starvation detector is now verified by a **replay harness** rather than by greps over the workflow text. Inverting the comparison the detector exists to protect (`-lt` → `-ge`) leaves the four grep steps **4 pass, 0 fail — blind**, while the harness fails **4 of 5 fixtures** and exits 1 (#541).

## ⚠️ Disclosures

Stated here because a green release can still have checked less than it appears to.

**This release shipped WITHOUT an independent review.** `FV-RELAY-REVIEW-140` — the `/code-review ultra` checkpoint that the approved release plan places before every tag — was **explicitly de-scoped by the maintainer on 2026-10-09** and moved to v1.141. The artifact was re-scoped rather than deleted, with its range **pinned** to `falcon-v1.139.0..falcon-v1.140.0`, so this diff is still reviewed before v1.141 tags rather than falling into a blind spot between two reviews. For calibration on what that gate catches: the equivalent review on v1.139 returned **nine findings**, including a `workflow_dispatch` input interpolated into a `run:` block on a self-hosted runner.

**29 traceability inverse links are unmeasured.** `rivet check bidirectional` fires with 29 missing `allocated-to` inverses (e.g. `SWARCH-FALCON-001 -(allocated-from)-> SWREQ-FALCON-ATT-P01`). This oracle is **not run by any CI workflow**, so it has never gated a release. It was not investigated before this tag and is recorded as open.

**A release-gate oracle was returning false blockers.** `rivet check verification-evidence` reports 96 of this repo's 183 named-test steps as citing tests that do not exist. **All 96 are false** — it matches filters as exact test names, while `cargo test <filter>` is a substring match over the full test path; one citation sampled per crate across all 12 affected crates exited 0 with tests passing. Filed as `pulseengine/rivet#1063`. Relay is insulated because its verification gate **executes** `fields.steps[].run` rather than name-matching them — but note that a bare `rivet check` prints help and exits 0, so wiring it in as a gate would pass vacuously.

**A clean-room review of this release exists, returned DO NOT TAG, and four of its five blocking findings are fixed — the fifth is not.** An independent cold-context review ran against v1.140 on 2026-10-01 (agent `a02291cfdd4bf4e2b`) and recommended against tagging. Its findings are reconciled here because a review whose verdict is not dispositioned in public is the same as no review:

| finding | disposition |
|---|---|
| `ENDURANCE-P01` — the 1 h gz hold had never run (`GZ_MAX_S` empty → 120 s), no wasm step existed, and `GZ_FLOOR_S: 25` let a 4.8× regression pass | **fixed** — #523 ratcheted the floor to 3600 s, #524 added the wasm path, #525 judges both paths horizontally |
| `BATTERY-P03` — its own falsification was met by a passing cited test; the text predated the #475/#476 correction | **fixed** — the text now reads "but only if it has ever had a pack", matching `batt_seen && batt_missing_s > BATT_SILENCE_S` |
| `FLEET-002` — could not fail; inverting the comparison left all four grep steps green, and no replay harness was committed | **fixed** — #541 landed the harness, #542 promoted it on the inversion measurement |
| `MIXPROOF-001` — steps exited 1 as written (missing `working-directory`) and the artifact was outside the gate's `(has-tag "falcon")` filter | **fixed** — steps now `cd crates/relay-mix-quad &&` and the `falcon` tag is present |
| `FV-FALCON-HOLD-001` — the verdict allows **2×** HOLD-P01's bounds | ⚠️ **OPEN — #546** |

The open one, stated precisely: HOLD-P01 requires the vehicle *"remain within 0.5 m vertically and 1.0 m horizontally … for at least 60 s"* — a bound at every instant. The verdict (`examples/falcon-sitl-gz/src/main.rs:2013`) checks the **final sample** at the requirement's bound, then sets every aggregate that could see a mid-run excursion at **twice** it: `rms_steady < 1.0` against a 0.5 m vertical bound, `peak_horiz < 2.0` against a 1.0 m horizontal one. A hold that excursions to 1.9 m at t=30 s and settles by t=60 s violates the requirement and passes its own `verified` verification.

**Nothing in this release is false on that account.** The measured margin is 14–60×: the scheduled soak reports peak excursions of 0.016–0.071 m against a 1.0 m bound. The defect is that the gate would not catch a regression until it was twice as bad as the requirement allows — the `VGATE` family's own pattern, *a green gate can check less than it claims*, applied to the flagship hold requirement.

It was not fixed before this tag deliberately. Tightening a required gate's bar deserves its own PR with its own mutation evidence — proving the tightened bar can still fail, and that both legs pass it on three runs rather than one — and the tag was authorized on specific content. Disclosing the gap beat silently expanding the release. Scoped v1.141 as #546.

Two further non-blocking observations from the same review are recorded for completeness: `BATT_SILENCE_S` can be set to 0.0 with all 66 `falcon-core` tests still green, so the clause "a single dropped sample cannot trigger the failsafe either" has no test pinning it from below; and `279b0c5` (#487) changed the estimator by +224 lines and edited `FV-FALCON-HOLD-001` in the same PR while leaving it `verified` — the two-commit script only catches status *transitions*, not edits to an already-verified artifact.

## Falsification statement

**This release is wrong if**, on either execution path, a one-hour position hold exceeds **1.0 m final horizontal error** or **2.0 m peak horizontal excursion** — the bars the nightly soak now enforces on both the native and wasm paths — or if the same hold, run on real 6X-RT silicon rather than the gz plant, shows the estimator diverging where the simulated plant does not. The second clause is the one this release cannot yet test: every number above comes from simulation, and no claim here has been measured on a vehicle.
